title: Paranormal group to host investigation at King Opera House in Van Buren | River Valley Democrat-Gazette
excerpt: VAN BUREN -- A small group of area residents will get to experience the paranormal in Van Buren on Friday at the King Opera House.
content:
VAN BUREN -- A small group of area residents will get to experience the paranormal in Van Buren on Friday at the King Opera House.

The Night Terror Collective, a Fort Smith-based paranormal investigation group, is hosting a small group investigation at the King Opera House. The event aims to help get residents into the paranormal and show off a real investigation.

Friday's event will only have 40 tickets available at $20 each, and the investigation begins at 8 p.m. at the opera house, 427 Main St.

Jason Walker, who teams with Rosy Page as part of the paranormal group, said the two travel around the country to various locations said to be haunted. Walker said he hosts these investigations across the country for a variety of reasons, including helping build interest in the paranormal.

"It's a chance for the public to come investigate with seasoned investigators and they can learn the difference from what they see on the TV shows to how an actual investigation works," Walker said.

Tickets for the investigation, which are still available, can be purchased online through Walker's Facebook page using electronic payments through Cashapp or Venmo, Walker said.

According to the city of Van Buren's website, the King Opera House is a Victorian-era performance hall in the city's downtown and was constructed in 1891.

The opera house is currently managed by the nonprofit Arts on Main after being turned over in 2022.

Walker said the King Opera House is very haunted and the spirits there are active, ranging from full bodied apparitions to disembodied voices, footsteps and noises of doors closing.

"This building has a rich history and a lot of energy," Walker said. "As to a specific spirit, who knows? When we open that door and let them in, in all honesty we don't know who we are communicating with. Sometimes they may give us a name, but a lot of the time, it's just an educational guess."

Stories of paranormal sightings and events at the opera house have been known since the early 1900s, according to Haunted Rooms Co., a company that offers tours of haunted locations.

The company's website states the ghost who haunts the opera house belongs to Charles Tolson, the lead of a weekly Vaudeville show staged in the building.

Tolson was shot after performing at the King Opera House just before getting on a train to Fort Smith, according to the website. Tolson had caught the eye of Allye Parchman, 17, who had dreams of leaving the small town with the actor, but her father caught the two at the train station and shot Tolson twice, the website states.

Eventually, Tolson died at Bell Point Hospital in Fort Smith on Oct. 5, 1903, according to the website.

The ghost of Tolson now is attached to the King Opera House, the site of his last venue before being murdered, the website says.

Sightings have included seeing Tolson dressed in a long black Victorian coat and top hat along with a cape, while other reports include people feeling watched and an employee coming back in the morning to find all the lights on after turning them off, according to the website.

Walker said his group is very experienced in what it does, The River Valley is lucky to have so much history and haunted locations, he said.

The area can hold its own against the most haunted locations in the country, Walker said.

This will be the first of three events at the King Opera House, with additional events planned for Oct. 23 and Nov. 13, although details are not yet confirmed on those, Walker said. People who are interested can watch his Facebook page for more information on those times, he added.

"It's really cool watching someone experience something truly paranormal for the first time," Walker said. "We have not hosted an event yet that was bad. The spirits participate when and if they want to. We can't make them do anything, and we wouldn't want to. It really all depends on them and if they want to communicate with us that particular night or not."
